Snap Up Properties at Bargain Prices in Cambria County, Pennsylvania

Grab properties at 40-90% below market value in Cambria County, Pennsylvania, through annual tax sales. These sales present a fantastic opportunity to acquire real estate at a fraction of its market value.

Cambria County Tax Sales Overview

  • Upset Sale: The Upset Sale happens annually after Labor Day. The county sells properties with all existing liens and judgments, usually scheduling this sale in September in Courtroom #1 of the Cambria County Courthouse. You must pre-register on the scheduled pre-registration date.
  • Judicial Sale: If properties don’t sell at the Upset Sale, they move to the Judicial Sale, where they are sold free of most liens and encumbrances.
  • Repository Sale: Unsold properties from the Judicial Sale are listed in the Repository Sale and can be bought without needing court approval.
  • Private Tax Sale: Occurs several times a year for properties not sold at the Upset Sale.

Payment and Registration Details

  • Payment Methods: Cash, personal check (with bank verification), certified check, or money order. Full payment is due on the day of sale.
  • Registration: Bidders must pre-register in person during the specified registration period. Forms and additional details are available on the Cambria County Tax Claim Department’s website.

Pro Tips for Tax Sale Success:

  1. Do Your Homework: Ensure you understand all conditions and terms of the sale. Check for liens or judgments on properties.
  2. Pre-register: Complete registration well in advance to avoid last-minute issues.
  3. Budget Wisely: Set a budget and stick to it during bidding to avoid overspending.
  4. Consult the Tax Claim Bureau: They can provide critical details and answer your questions.

Attractions and Economic Highlights in Cambria County:

  • Popular Attractions: Visit parks, theatres, and historic sites.
  • Transportation: Well-developed road and rail networks with nearby airports.
  • Economic Development: Growth in sectors like agriculture, technology, mining, and manufacturing.
  • Community Appeal: Outdoor recreational activities, entertainment options, eco-tourism, and historical attractions.

FAQs about Cambria County Tax Sales

What is an Upset Sale?
An Upset Sale auctions properties with delinquent taxes, selling them along with all existing liens and judgments.

How do I register for the sale?
You must pre-register in person at the Tax Claim Bureau office.

What payment methods are accepted?
Buyers use cash, personal checks (with verification), certified checks, or money orders to make payments.

Where can I find more information?
Visit the Cambria County Tax Claim Department for detailed information and forms.
